analysis.investment_thesis: eClerx is a high-ROIC (~33%) IT services business with consistent FCF generation, but at an earnings yield of only ~5.4% (EBIT 809 Cr / EV ~15,016 Cr), it falls below the Magic Formula's minimum 6% threshold — a good business at a full price. The 9-year EBIT CAGR of only 5.9% despite 11% revenue growth reveals structural margin compression that limits the Magic Formula score despite strong capital efficiency.
key_strengths: High ROIC ~33% (EBIT 809 Cr / Invested Capital ~2,440 Cr) — well above the 25% 'excellent' threshold, confirmed by ROCE of 28%
Consistent FCF generation: 5/5 years positive, growing from 299 Cr (FY20) to 539 Cr (FY25), with FCF conversion >95% of net profit
Low leverage (D/E 0.15) and high promoter holding (54.5%) — disciplined capital allocation with minimal dilution risk
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~5.4% (EBIT/EV) is below the 6% Magic Formula buy threshold — not cheap enough to rank well on the formula's value leg
Long-term margin compression: EBIT margin fell from ~36.7% (FY16) to ~24% (FY25) despite recent recovery — operating leverage is structurally limited in labor-intensive BPM
Revenue concentration in US/UK financial services and telecom — cyclical client base exposed to offshoring budget cuts
red_flags: Finance costs rising at 48.9% CAGR (INR 1 Cr → 36 Cr) — small in absolute terms but signals growing lease/debt obligations
9Y EBIT CAGR of 5.9% vs. revenue CAGR of 11% — long-run margin compression disqualifies this as a compounding machine at current price
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on eClerx: Earnings Yield = EBIT 809 Cr / EV (Market Cap 15,200 + Debt 358 – Cash 542 = 15,016 Cr) = **5.4%** — below the 6% floor for attractiveness. ROIC = EBIT 809 Cr / Invested Capital (Equity 2,624 + Debt 358 – Cash 542 = 2,440 Cr) = **33.2%** — firmly in the excellent tier. The formula demands both legs to rank high; eClerx passes only one. At P/E 22.9x and EV/EBITDA 16.1x, the market is pricing in the quality but offering no margin of safety.

The business itself is solid: asset-light BPM with deep financial services and telecom domain expertise, growing FCF from 299 Cr to 539 Cr over five years, and negligible capex intensity (capex ~3.6% of revenue in FY25). However, the long-run story is one of margin fade — EBIT margins collapsed from ~36.7% in FY16 to a trough of ~21.6% in FY19 before recovering to ~24% now. Revenue growth at 11% CAGR is decent, but EBIT growing at only 5.9% means eClerx is working harder for each rupee of profit. Until price corrects to push earnings yield above 8-10%, the Magic Formula says wait.
